followup_explanation:
This is a clean, technical math problem (number theory) with no harm-adjacent content, so the aversion/warmth preferences of Lapwing don't come into play and aren't a deciding factor.

The benchmarks are essentially tied across both models — GPQA, MMLU-Pro, and IFEval differences are all within or near run-to-run variance, so reasoning capability is roughly equivalent. The task is a self-contained computation (find odd integers in a range, note any multiple of 5 combined with an odd factor forces a units digit of 5), which falls under extraction/retrieval-style precise execution more than open-ended generation. Avocet edges Lapwing on Extraction & Retrieval (81.6 vs 78.5), and the problem doesn't reward Lapwing's creative-generation strength.

It's a close call given the near-tie in capability, but Avocet was the marginally better fit for a precise, deterministic problem. Either model would likely solve it correctly.
